hero.subtitle: built from scratch

points: One core user journey built end to end, for example sign up, book, pay and get a confirmation.

points: Scope is fixed on day one. Anything that doesn't serve the core journey goes on the v2 list.

steps.title: Days 3–7: Build

points: Production deploy, analytics, handover and a plan for the next sprint.

faqs.question: Can you really build an MVP in 10 days?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the scope is one focused product journey. We agree that scope on day one and keep a written v2 list for everything else. Larger platforms are delivered as a series of sprints, each ending with something live.

faqs.question: Do I own the code?
faqs.answer: Yes. The code is in your repository and deployed to accounts you own from day one.

faqs.question: What happens after the first 10 days?
faqs.answer: Most clients continue with follow-up sprints or a monthly retainer, adding features based on what real users do. You can also take the code to your own team.

faqs.question: What do you need from me to start?
faqs.answer: A clear idea of who the product is for and the main problem it solves, plus about 30 minutes a day for quick decisions during the sprint.

faqs.question: What is the difference between native and cross-platform apps?
faqs.answer: Native apps are built separately for iOS and Android using platform-specific code, offering the best performance, while cross-platform apps share one codebase across both platforms, reducing cost and development time. Fajraan Tech builds both depending on the project's goals.

faqs.question: Should I build my app with Flutter or React Native?
faqs.answer: Flutter and React Native both allow a single codebase to run on iOS and Android. Flutter tends to offer more consistent UI across platforms, while React Native integrates well with existing JavaScript teams. Fajraan Tech recommends the right framework based on your app's requirements and team skillset.
